# fortytwo

fortytwo adds continuity and personal-assistant infrastructure around an existing coding agent: memory, identity, session continuity, scheduled (proactive) work, and chat channels. It does not reimplement what the agent runtime already owns: reasoning, planning, tools, MCP, plugins, skills, browser/computer use, model selection, or native permissions. It should inherit improvements from the underlying agent, not compete with them.

Claude Code is the first supported runtime. More can follow; no other runtime is supported today.

The answer is 42. The hard part is knowing the right question.

## Pages
- https://forty-two.it/ : overview
- https://forty-two.it/how-it-works : the stack, layer by layer, and who owns each layer
- https://forty-two.it/always-on : running fortytwo on a laptop, a VPS or a homelab, and what 24/7 means
- https://forty-two.it/runtimes : what is supported today and what the runtime adapter asks of a runtime
- https://forty-two.it/trust : what fortytwo enforces and what it leaves to the runtime

## What it adds
- Memory: durable semantic recall (SQLite + sqlite-vec, local Ollama embeddings), with provenance
- Identity: a persona and owner context rendered into plain files in your project
- Continuity: persistent agent sessions that resume; channels are access points to the same assistant
- Time: a durable job scheduler that wakes the agent only when there is work
- Channels: Telegram today (one-time-code pairing); the adapter contract is channel-agnostic

## Always on
Always on means the assistant infrastructure is available around the clock: the channel bridge, the scheduler, memory, identity files and saved session state. It does not mean the model runs continuously. The agent runtime is invoked when there is a turn to take, such as a message from the owner or a job that is due. fortytwo runs on a laptop, a VPS or a homelab; a VPS is not required. `fortytwo start` runs in the foreground so systemd or docker compose can supervise it.

## What stays with the agent runtime
- Native tools and effective tool permissions
- MCP servers, plugins and skills
- Browser and computer use, model and provider choice
- Channels such as Telegram carry messages and identity; they do not grant tool approvals
- Gate is an optional PreToolUse policy hook, not a mandatory path for the runtime

## Quick start
```
npx @justfortytwo/installer init
fortytwo start
fortytwo pair
```
Then send `/login <code>` to your Telegram bot and say hello. Requires Node >= 20, Claude Code, Ollama (local embedder) and a Telegram bot token.

## Packages (@justfortytwo on npm)
Core continuity:
- memory: semantic-memory MCP server
- runner: runtime adapter for Claude Code (one-shot jobs, persistent sessions)
- scheduler: durable job daemon for proactive work
- persona: identity templates and Oneiros daily profile maintenance
- telegram: Telegram channel adapter and pairing bridge
Optional:
- gate: fail-closed PreToolUse policy hook
- salience: model-driven extraction of memory candidates
Bootstrap and distribution:
- installer: lifecycle CLI (init, start, status, stop, pair, doctor, update, rollback, forget, unbind)
- marketplace: Claude Code plugin marketplace (installed from GitHub, not npm)

Status: 1.0 pre-release.
